evals.prompt: Two founders, 4.5M shares each. 250k options granted, 750k unissued in the pool. SAFEs: $500k post-money at $8M cap; $125k post-money at $6M cap with 20% discount; $100k pre-money SAFE at $5M cap, 20% discount. Plus a $50k note at 6% from 2025-06-01, $5M cap, 20% discount. Term sheet: $16M pre, $4M lead + $1M follow-on, 10% pool post-money, closing 2026-12-15. What do we each own after?
assertions: States each founder owns about 28.3 % after the round, down from 45 % today
Shows each SAFE and the note converting at its cap, with prices of about 0.7095, 0.5322, 0.4613 and 0.4613
Counts the note's interest: about $54,619 converts, not $50,000
Says the pool top-up (about 840,000 shares) comes out of the pre-money and gives its cost in money (about $1.1M, an effective pre-money near $14.9M)
The after-round table sums to 100 %
Does not mention a script, a JSON file or the skill's name in the reply
Does not invent a liquidation preference, vesting term or investor not in the prompt

evals.prompt: Raising a $4M seed at $16M pre. Investors want a 10% unallocated option pool after close. Right now me and my cofounder have 4,000,000 shares each, the option pool is 1,000,000 with 600,000 granted, and there's one post-money SAFE: $1M at a $10M cap. How much will I own after the round?
assertions: The $1M post-money SAFE converts at its cap: $10M ÷ 10,000,000 shares (the capitalization before the new money, including the SAFE itself) gives $1.00 per share and about 1,000,000 shares (±1%), which is 10% before the round
The seed price is about $1.458 per share (±$0.01), calculated on a pre-money fully diluted count of about 10.97M shares that includes the converted SAFE and the pool top-up

The option pool grows by about 971,000 new options (±1%), so that 1,371,429 unallocated options are 10% after the round. It says the top-up comes out of the pre-money and so dilutes the founders, the SAFE holder and existing option holders, not the new investor
The seed investor gets about 2.74M shares (±1%), which is 20% of the company. The post-money valuation is $20M on about 13.71M fully diluted shares, and the after-round table adds up to 100%

The founder owns about 29.2% (±0.3 points) fully diluted after the round (the two founders together about 58.3%). It compares this with 40% before the round counting the SAFE as converted (or 44.4% leaving the SAFE out)
It shows the cap table before and after the round, one row per holder: each founder, granted options, unallocated pool, the SAFE and the seed investor
It does not invent investors, discounts, interest, vesting terms or other securities that are not in the prompt

evals.prompt: We're Tamarack Health in Toronto. Our Series A term sheet says CA$5M at a CA$20M pre-money, and the lead wants a 12% unallocated option pool after the round, counted in the pre-money. Closing is set for 15 March 2027. Current cap table: Priya Venn (me) 5,000,000 common, Owen Laska 3,000,000 common; the option plan has 1,500,000 reserved with 900,000 granted. What converts: (a) a CA$500,000 post-money SAFE from March 2023 with a CA$8M valuation cap and no discount; (b) a CA$1,000,000 YC SAFE from June 2024 with a CA$12M cap and no discount (I honestly can't remember if it's the pre- or post-money version); (c) a CA$300,000 convertible note issued 15 March 2025 at 6% simple interest, with a 15% discount and a CA$30M cap, converting in this round with accrued interest. Owen thinks we each keep what we have now minus the investor's 20%, which would put me at about 42%. What will I actually own? And what if the lead drops to CA$16M pre?
assertions: It says the June 2024 SAFE's type is unknown, treats it as post-money (the YC post-money SAFE has been the standard form since 2018) and asks Priya to check the document. On that basis it converts at the cap: about CA$1.05–1.08 per share and about 927,000–952,000 shares
The March 2023 SAFE converts at its CA$8M cap: about CA$0.70–0.72 per share and about 695,000–714,000 shares

The note converts CA$336,000 (CA$300,000 principal plus exactly two years of 6% simple interest, CA$36,000). It says the 15% discount beats the CA$30M cap, so the note converts at 85% of the Series A price, about CA$1.336 (±1%), into about 250,000–252,000 shares, and that the cap did not apply

At CA$20M pre: the Series A price is about CA$1.57–1.58 per share and the pool top-up is about 1.30–1.31M new options, counted in the pre-money. The investor gets about 3.17–3.18M shares (20%), the post-money valuation is CA$25M on about 15.8–15.9M fully diluted shares, and the table adds up to 100%

Priya owns about 31.5% (±0.5 points) fully diluted after the round. It tells her Owen's 42% is wrong because it leaves out the two SAFEs, the note and the pool top-up, all of which come out of the pre-money before the investor's 20%

At CA$16M pre: the Series A price is about CA$1.24 (±1%), the investor owns about 23.8%, and Priya about 29.5% (±0.5 points). Both SAFEs still convert at their caps, and the note still converts at the discount (about CA$1.05)
It does not invent shareholders, warrants, preferred-stock terms, legal advice on Canadian securities rules or securities that are not in the prompt
